message.reasoning_content:
The image shows an Audemars Piguet Royal Oak, blue dial with "Grande Tapisserie" pattern, steel bracelet. Looks like ref 15500ST.OO.1220ST.01 (41mm, blue dial) — but the dial looks slightly smaller relative... Actually the date window at 3 o'clock, applied AP logo at 12. The 15500ST has a date at 3. The 15400ST also. The 15500 has no "AP" logo applied... Actually the 15500 has applied gold AP logo at 12 and "AUDEMARS PIGUET" printed below. The 15400 has "AP" logo printed. Here the logo appears printed/small "AP" above AUDEMARS PIGUET — that's the 15400 style. Hmm, in the 15500, the AP monogram is applied above the printed AUDEMARS PIGUET. In 15400, the AP logo is printed directly above... Both have small AP monogram. Hard to distinguish.

The 15500 dial has the "AUDEMARS PIGUET" text and the outer track with minute markers, and the date at 3 with no printed quarter numerals... Actually 15500 removed the "AP" applied? Let me recall: 15500ST has applied AP monogram at 12, printed AUDEMARS PIGUET beneath, and "AUTOMATIC" printed above the 6. The 15400ST has AP monogram printed (?) Actually 15400 has applied "AP" logo too. Hmm.

The key difference: 15500 has date at 3 without frame and larger; the 15400 has date window at 3 with a frame. Also, 15500 dial lacks "AUTOMATIC" text? No, 15500 has "AUTOMATIC" at 6. 15400 also has "AUTOMATIC".

Wrist size: it looks like 41mm on a large wrist. I'll go with 15500ST.OO.1220ST.01 as the most common current blue dial Royal Oak, or 15400ST.OO.1220ST.01.

The blue dial Grande Tapisserie with date at 3 — the 15500's dial has a "sunburst" blue with Grande Tapisserie. I'll pick 15500ST.OO.1220ST.01, confidence ~0.5.

Actually, in the photo the AP monogram at 12 appears as a small applied logo with "AUDEMARS PIGUET" text below — consistent with both. The date window is at 3 slightly inset. I'll go with 15500ST.OO.1220ST.01.

Movement: automatic (Calibre 4302). Case: stainless steel. Bracelet: metal (steel). Confidence 0.5.
